D012-D016_h001.question:
It’s a bit embarrassing at my age, but I’ve been having these reactions to spiders for… I’d say the last few months, maybe longer, but it’s gotten worse recently. I deliver mail, so I’m in and out of garden gates, sheds, porches. If I see a spider, especially the bigger ones, it’s like something just snaps in me straight away. My chest tightens, my heart races, my hands get sweaty. Sometimes I feel like I can’t catch my breath for a minute or two, like I have to get away right then.

It’s not that I’m thinking anything super specific, it’s more this rush of “something bad” without really knowing what exactly. At home, my wife jokes because I’ll stand there staring at a spider on the wall, sort of frozen, checking it over and over to see if it’s moved, instead of just dealing with it. On my route, if I know a house has lots of webs, I’ll hesitate or take a longer way round, but I still do the job. I keep wondering if I’m overreacting or if there’s something else going on.
D012-D016_h001.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h001.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h002.question:
It’s been… I’m not even sure, maybe a few months? I started noticing it more this past storm season. When the weather turns or there’s a really heavy rain, especially at night, something in me just locks up. If I’m at home and the wind picks up, I’ll find myself standing by the window or in the hallway, just stuck there, like my body won’t cooperate. It’s not like a little worry; it’s more like my brain goes blank and all I can do is listen to the wind and wait for it to pass.

Working at the gallery, I’ve caught myself checking the forecast a lot during the day, especially if I know I’ll be going home late and it’ll be dark and possibly raining. Sometimes I’ll stay longer at work or leave earlier, just to avoid walking outside when it’s really bad out. Other times I tell myself I’m being ridiculous and go anyway, but my heart’s pounding and I feel rooted to the spot when the gusts hit or it suddenly gets very dark. It’s unpredictable—some days I manage fine, other days it feels overwhelming.
D012-D016_h002.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h002.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h003.question:
I guess the main thing bothering me is this intense reaction I have to spiders, and honestly most bugs. It’s been more noticeable the last few months. I work in the tower, and even just imagining one crawling near my headset or on the console can make my chest tighten and my palms sweat. Sometimes I’ll be halfway through a shift and suddenly picture one under the desk and I lose focus for a minute, just kind of frozen.

At home, if I see something that even looks like a spider, I’ll jump up, check the corners, under the couch, around the windows. I’ll stand there staring at it from a distance, trying to decide what to do, replaying different “what if” scenarios in my head—like, what if it crawls on the kids, or ends up in the bedroom. Even when there’s nothing there, I sometimes find myself scanning certain spots over and over, just to be sure.

I know it sounds over the top for something so small, and part of me knows it’s not logical, but the feeling in the moment is very real and hard to shut off.
D012-D016_h003.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h003.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h004.question:
It’s been maybe… I don’t know, a year or so that this has really started to bother me. I work in a plant with a lot of high platforms and catwalks, and lately just knowing I might have to go up there gets my chest tight. If I look down from the higher levels, my legs feel kind of rubbery and I get this rush in my head, like I might lose control somehow. 

Even when I’m at home, if I know there’s a job coming up that involves the upper walkways, I find myself going over it in my mind again and again the night before, picturing being up there, and I can’t settle down. I lie in bed thinking, “What if something happens up there?” and I get that same nervous feeling just from imagining it.

It’s not like I refuse to go up at all, but I dread it. Sometimes I take longer routes around the plant so I don’t have to think about the higher areas. My wife says I’m more on edge, especially when the weather’s bad and there’s talk of storms rolling in; I catch myself staring at the sky and feeling uneasy for no clear reason.
D012-D016_h004.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h004.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h005.question:
I’ve been having a lot of trouble with certain things in the environment, mostly at night and when the weather turns bad. It’s been going on for… I’d say at least several months, maybe longer, but it’s gotten worse lately.

I work nights as a security guard, so I’m often outside in the dark. Sometimes, when I step out to do a round and it’s really dark, or if I hear the wind pick up like a storm’s coming, my body just reacts. My chest starts pounding, I feel like I can’t get a full breath, my hands get sweaty, and my legs feel a bit shaky. It can come on pretty suddenly, even if nothing is actually happening.

If there’s talk of heavy rain or a storm, I catch myself thinking about it a lot beforehand, kind of bracing for it. I don’t always avoid going out—my job doesn’t really allow that—but I might delay stepping outside or double-check things more than I probably need to. My wife says I seem on edge on those nights.
D012-D016_h005.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h005.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h006.question:
It’s mostly with elevators and tunnels, and sometimes those long, high bridges. It’s been going on… I’d say at least several months, maybe longer, but it’s really started to bother me this past year.

If I know we’re going somewhere that might have an elevator, I start getting tense ahead of time—my chest feels tight, my hands get sweaty. When I’m actually in the elevator or in a tunnel, it hits me all at once: my heart starts pounding, I feel like I can’t get a full breath, and I have this rush of “I need to get out now.” It’s not just nerves; it’s like my body is in full-on alarm mode.

I can’t always avoid it. If I’ve got the kids with me and we’re at the doctor’s office or at a mall garage, sometimes the elevator is the only realistic option. So I ride it, but I’m gripping the stroller or the rail, counting the seconds, trying to look calm for the kids while inside I’m terrified and just waiting for the doors to open. Afterward I feel exhausted and a bit embarrassed, like I should be able to handle something so ordinary.
D012-D016_h006.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D012-D016_h006.answer: B & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h007.question:
It’s mostly anything medical that sets me off. I work as a sign language interpreter, so sometimes I’m in hospitals or clinics with clients. Over the past… maybe a year or two, I’ve noticed that if I even catch a glimpse of blood, or see someone getting a shot, my whole body just locks up. It’s like I freeze on the spot. I can still sign, but it feels mechanical, like I’m moving through molasses.

I don’t actually pass out, but my heart races, my hands shake, and I feel this wave of dread. I keep telling myself, “Just get through this, you have to stay professional,” so I don’t walk out of the room. I force myself to stay, because leaving would mess up the appointment for the patient I’m interpreting for, but the whole time I’m just bracing myself and trying not to look directly at what’s happening.

It’s gotten to the point where I’ll replay those scenes in my head afterward and worry about the next appointment, but I’m not sure if it’s just normal anxiety or something else.
D012-D016_h007.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D012-D016_h007.answer: B & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h008.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time with anything to do with blood or medical stuff for… I’d say at least the last couple of years, getting worse this past year.  

If I know I might have to get a blood test or a jab, I start getting worked up days beforehand. My heart races just reading one of those appointment letters. Sometimes I’ll picture the needle or the blood and feel light‑headed, like I might keel over, even when I’m just sitting at home.  

Because of that, I’ve put off going to the GP more than once, even when my wife nags me about my knees or my blood pressure. I walk miles every day for the post, but if I see the mobile blood donation van parked near my route, I’ll actually cross the street or change the order of my deliveries so I don’t have to go near it.  

I’m not sure if I’m overreacting or if there’s something else going on in my head, but it’s getting to the point where I avoid things I probably shouldn’t, just to not deal with it.
D012-D016_h008.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D012-D016_h008.answer: B & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h009.question:
I guess the main thing is how I react in certain situations, especially elevators and those long, tight tunnels in parking garages. I work from home as a writer, so I can usually arrange my life to avoid them, but when I have to go into the city for a meeting or to see friends, it becomes a whole production.

The second I step toward a closed elevator, my chest tightens, my heart just slams, and I get this rush of “I need to get out of here” before I’ve even gone in. Sometimes I’ll still make myself take it if people are waiting behind me or there’s no easy stairway. I’ll stand in the back, gripping my bag, trying to look normal while my mind runs through all these horrible “what if” scenarios and I feel like I might faint or lose control.

It’s been like this, off and on, for maybe a year or so. I don’t completely avoid those places, but I dread them, and when I can’t get around them, I feel trapped and shaky the whole time until it’s over.
D012-D016_h009.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D012-D016_h009.answer: B & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h010.question:
It’s a little hard to explain cleanly. I’m a PGY‑2 in surgery, so I’m around all kinds of things all the time, but there’s this weird issue with certain animals and bugs that’s been getting to me.

The main thing is spiders, but sometimes bees too. If one shows up in the call room or even if I see one near the entrance when I’m coming into the hospital, my body just… flips. Heart racing, palms sweaty, my chest feels tight, like I’m about to be stuck or attacked, even though I know that’s not logical. It’s almost instantaneous—one second I’m fine, the next I’m on high alert.

I don’t actually run away, because I can’t; I’m scrubbed in, or I’m on call, or I’m the senior in the room, so I just kind of freeze and force myself to keep going, but inside I’m panicking. I’ll keep glancing back to make sure it hasn’t moved closer, and it gets hard to focus on what I’m doing.

This has been happening off and on for maybe the past several months. I can still do my job, but it’s really distracting and embarrassing.
D012-D016_h010.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D012-D016_h010.answer: B & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h011.question:
I’ve been really on edge about anything medical for maybe… I don’t know, around a year? It’s gotten worse the last few months. If someone even talks about getting blood drawn at the salon, my stomach flips and I feel lightheaded, like I might pass out. I avoid looking at their pictures or videos if they show me anything from the hospital. I’ll pretend I have another client just so I can walk away.

I skipped my last check-up because I knew they might want blood tests. I told the receptionist I was sick, but really I just couldn’t make myself go. Even scrolling on my phone, if I see something that looks like it might show blood or an injection, I swipe past super fast. I don’t even watch medical shows anymore.

Sometimes I get stuck thinking about it afterwards — like replaying it in my head, worrying something bad might happen if I don’t stay away from that stuff. I’m not sure if I’m overreacting or if there’s something else going on, but it’s starting to mess with normal things, like just going to the doctor when I need to.
D012-D016_h011.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D012-D016_h011.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h012.question:
I’m not really sure how to explain it, but something about storms and heavy rain has been getting to me over the past several months, maybe around half a year. I work nights sometimes at the hospital, and if there’s a forecast for a big storm, I’ll go out of my way to switch shifts or stay over on a couch rather than go home. It’s not just getting wet—it’s the wind, the thunder, the way the sky looks. I feel this rush of anxiety, like something terrible is going to happen, even though I can’t say exactly what.

I’ve started checking the weather app a lot, sometimes over and over in a short time, especially on days I’m supposed to commute. If it shows any chance of a storm, I’ll cancel plans, skip the gym, or avoid going out for groceries. My friends have stopped inviting me to certain things because I always say, “It might rain.” I know it sounds irrational, and I keep wondering if I’m overreacting or missing something, but I just can’t seem to shake it.
D012-D016_h012.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D012-D016_h012.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h013.question:
I’ve been having this thing with storms for maybe a year or so now, and it’s getting harder to shrug off. I’m out driving a lot for showings, and if I see those dark clouds rolling in or get a weather alert on my phone, my stomach just drops. My mind kind of jumps ahead to all the things that could go wrong—flooded roads, trees coming down, power going out when I’m alone at home.

I still go to appointments, even when the radar looks bad, but the whole time I’m on edge. My heart races, my hands get sweaty on the steering wheel, and I’m constantly checking the sky, the wipers, the route on my GPS, almost in a loop. I’ll replay the forecast in my head—did they say “severe” or just “scattered”?—over and over.

At night, if I know a storm’s supposed to come through, I don’t sleep well. I keep glancing at my phone, listening for thunder, half expecting something terrible to happen, even though nothing actually has. It feels over the top, but I can’t seem to just brush it off.
D012-D016_h013.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D012-D016_h013.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h014.question:
I guess the main thing is this… it’s about spiders. I work for the council, so I’m around rubbish heaps, sheds, old containers all the time. If I even think there might be spiders, my whole body just goes on edge. My heart starts thumping, my hands sweat, and I get this tingling in my face, like I’m bracing for something horrible.

I still do the job – I don’t walk off site or anything – but sometimes I’ll stand there for a bit, trying to psych myself up before opening a bin or going into a dark storeroom. I’ll hold my breath, move really slowly, check corners over and over. If I see even a small one, I feel almost frozen, but I keep going because I have to. Afterwards I feel wrung out, sort of shaky and embarrassed.

At home my wife teases me a bit, but I’ve started asking her or the kids to deal with anything that looks “spidery.” This has been going on for years, but it’s gotten more noticeable to me over the last few months, like it’s taking more effort to push through it.
D012-D016_h014.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D012-D016_h014.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h015.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time with certain places and situations for… I guess at least several months now, maybe longer. It’s become more obvious since I started working at the café.

Anything that feels tight or hard to get out of really freaks me out—like elevators, long tunnels on the subway, or walking over those big bridges where you’re kind of stuck in the middle. Even crowded, enclosed spaces in the mall bother me. Sometimes it’s more like a strong discomfort, other times I feel this rush in my chest and I just need to get out.

Because of that, I plan my whole day around avoiding those situations. I leave home super early so I can take the longer bus route instead of the subway, even if it means less sleep. I refuse shifts that would require me to use the delivery elevator at work, which annoys my manager. I’ve skipped going out with friends if I know we’ll have to cross the bridge or use certain stations.  

I’m not totally sure why it feels so intense—there’s just this sense that something will go wrong and I won’t be able to handle it, so I do whatever I can to not end up there.
D012-D016_h015.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D012-D016_h015.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h016.question:
I’m a chef, so I’m used to stress, but this feels different. For about the last six months, I’ve had this intense reaction to being near deep water or really dark, open outdoor spaces. If my wife suggests a beach day or a late walk by the river, I start feeling sick to my stomach even before we leave the house. Just picturing it on the way home from work is enough to make my chest tighten and my palms sweat.

I go out of my way to avoid it now. If we’re driving and there’s a route that goes over a big bridge, I’ll add ten, fifteen minutes to the trip just to skip it. When we book vacations, I insist on places that are “more city, less nature,” and I make excuses so it doesn’t sound weird.

What worries me is that it’s not just when I’m actually there—my mind kind of gets stuck on “what if” scenarios. I replay them in my head, and once that starts, it’s really hard to shut it off, even when I’m trying to focus on service in the kitchen.
D012-D016_h016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D012-D016_h016.answer: D & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h017.question:
It’s a little hard to explain cleanly. I write from home, so in theory I can control my environment, but lately it feels like my environment is controlling me.

Nighttime is the worst. Once it gets fully dark, I just…lock up. If I have to cross my living room to shut a window or grab something from the kitchen, I sometimes literally stop halfway and can’t make myself move. It’s like my body forgets how to go forward. I stand there holding my breath until I can sort of talk myself out of it.

I’ve reorganized my whole life around not being out after sunset. I turn down evening client calls, I stopped going to my writing group because they meet at night, and I rush errands so I’m home before it gets dim. I know it sounds irrational even as I’m doing it, but I can’t shake this sense that something awful will happen if I don’t stick to these “rules” I’ve made up about when and how I move around in the dark.

This has been gradually ramping up over the past several months, enough that it’s starting to interfere with work and seeing people.
D012-D016_h017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D012-D016_h017.answer: D & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h018.question:
It’s been maybe a few months now that this has really started bothering me. I drive the city bus, so I’m out on the road all day, and I keep getting this rush of fear around certain animals, especially dogs and sometimes insects like bees. 

It’s not like I’m always scared of them, but every so often, if a dog suddenly comes close to the bus when I’m boarding passengers, I feel myself just lock up for a second. My hands kind of freeze on the wheel or on the door controls, like my body doesn’t want to move. I’m aware of it, and I hate that feeling, but I still have to open the doors and keep things moving, so I push through it while my heart is pounding and I’m tense all over.

Same thing if a bee gets inside the bus. I’ll keep driving and act normal for the passengers, but inside I’m really on edge, hyper-focused on where it is, trying not to react. I don’t skip my routes or anything, but I feel this constant dread that something like that will happen again.
D012-D016_h018.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D012-D016_h018.answer: D & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h019.question:
It’s a bit hard to explain cleanly. I’ve been out here at the station about four years, and I started noticing this maybe… a year or so ago? It’s not constant, but when it hits, it’s bad.

Any time I have to go through certain tight spaces on the supply ship—like the narrow stairwell down to the lower deck, or that little metal corridor that feels closed in—something in me just surges. My chest tightens, my heart starts hammering, and I get this rush like I’m going to lose control or faint if I don’t get out. It happens almost the instant I see where I have to go.

I’ve never actually refused outright, but I’ll only do it if I’m clutching my radio or my old pocket torch, and if one of the crew is right there in front of me or behind me. I focus on the click of the torch in my hand, or their footsteps, and just try to push through. If I’m alone in those spots, I feel like I can’t trust myself to handle it, so I usually find some excuse to wait or go another way if I can.
D012-D016_h019.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D012-D016_h019.answer: D & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h020.question:
I’ve been driving trucks for over twenty years, long routes all over the country, and I’ve always been fine on the road. But for maybe the last few months, certain parts of the trip really get to me, especially long tunnels and those high, narrow bridges.

When I see one coming up, it’s like my body locks up before I even get there. My hands go rigid on the wheel, my legs feel like concrete, and for a moment I’m not sure I can keep going. A couple of times I’ve had to pull over on the shoulder before the tunnel or take some long detour just to avoid going through. I’ll plan my routes around those spots now, even if it adds hours.

I can’t really tell if it’s the tunnel or bridge itself that scares me, or some thought about what might happen while I’m in there. It’s more like this wave of “something bad is going to happen” that hits me and I just freeze. I haven’t told my boss everything, just that I “don’t like” certain routes, but it’s starting to mess with my work and I’m worried it’ll get worse.
D012-D016_h020.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D012-D016_h020.answer: D & C. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h021.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, maybe a year or so that this has really started to mess with me. I work the line, I’m used to knives and minor cuts, but lately if someone slices a finger and there’s a bit more blood, I feel this wave hit me. My chest tightens, my vision sort of narrows, and I have to grab the prep table or lean on the counter. Sometimes I feel like I might pass out, so I call my wife or text her just to feel “grounded,” or I’ll keep my hand on my wedding ring and sort of rub it without really thinking.

It’s not just at work. If a medical show comes on and they’re drawing blood or doing some kind of procedure, I have to look away or leave the room. When I had to get a routine blood test a few months back, I only got through it because my wife came with me and sat right next to me. I kept talking to her and staring at the floor. I’m not even sure what exactly I’m afraid will happen; I just know I really don’t want to be in those situations, and when I can’t avoid them, I cling to anything that makes me feel safer.
D012-D016_h021.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D012-D016_h021.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h022.question:
I work nights moderating videos, mostly violent stuff, and for about… I don’t know, maybe the last 5–6 months, I’ve developed this really intense reaction to people vomiting. Not just actually seeing it in real life—sometimes just a clip starting to hint at it, or even someone saying they feel sick, makes my whole body go tight. My heart races, I feel like I can’t swallow properly, and I have to click away or rip my headphones off.

It’s gotten to the point where I avoid certain queues at work and beg coworkers to swap tasks if I think a batch might have that kind of content. I’ve turned down extra shifts and I’m behind on my quota because I pause so much, double-checking thumbnails, muting audio, or taking breaks to “calm down.” I also dodge parties, bars, even long bus rides, because I’m worried someone might get sick near me. Friends think I’m being dramatic, so I mostly just make excuses and stay home.

I’m not totally sure why this started now; I keep replaying stuff in my head, but I can’t tell if I’m overreacting or if something’s actually wrong.
D012-D016_h022.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D012-D016_h022.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h023.question:
It’s been maybe… eight, nine months that this has really started to mess with me. I do content around travel and “day in my life” stuff, so I’m constantly filming in different places, but anything to do with nature at night or big open water just freaks me out now.

Like, if I’m near the ocean at dusk for a shoot, my heart starts pounding, my chest feels tight, and I can’t stop scanning the water. Same with those cliff viewpoints or rooftop pools brands always want—my legs go shaky, and I get this urge to just get away from the edge or from the water, but I usually push through because it’s my job and people are watching. I’m smiling for the camera, but inside I feel like I’m going to lose it.

When I’m staying somewhere unfamiliar and it gets really dark outside, I’ll sit there replaying all the things that “could” happen. I don’t know if it’s just me overthinking because of all the hate I get online, or something else, but it’s intense enough that I dread certain shoots even though I still force myself to do them.
D012-D016_h023.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D012-D016_h023.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h024.question:
I’ve always been a bit jumpy, but in the last few months it’s started to feel like it’s running my day. The main thing is with spiders and, to a lesser extent, other bugs. If I even think I saw one in my apartment, I’ll sort of lock up and then I have to leave the room. Sometimes I’ll sleep on the couch because I’m convinced there’s one in my bedroom even if I can’t find anything.

I go out of my way to avoid places where I might run into them—like I won’t sit in the grass at the park with my friends anymore, and I refuse ground‑floor Airbnbs for work trips. At the office, if I see anything that looks like a spider near my desk, I’ll move to another workstation and I can’t really concentrate until I’m away from that spot.

What bothers me is I’m not even sure why it feels so intense. Part of me knows it’s over the top, but once the idea is in my head, it’s hard to shake and I just end up avoiding whatever might trigger it.

D012-D016_h025.question:
It’s mainly this thing with tunnels and those long underpasses on the highway. I’m fine most of the time, but as soon as we’re about to go into one, my whole body tenses up. My chest feels tight, my hands get sweaty, and I just stare straight ahead waiting for it to be over. It’s been happening off and on for maybe a year or so, getting more noticeable this semester since I’ve been driving more for school and practice.

If I’m alone, I’ll sometimes take a longer way around just so I don’t have to go through. If I can’t avoid it, I’ll call someone and keep them on speaker, or I’ll hold onto this keychain my little sister gave me. I know it sounds kind of dumb, but it makes me feel a bit less on edge, like I’m not totally by myself.

I keep running through “what if” scenarios in my head right before we go in, but I’m not even sure exactly what I think is going to happen. It’s not like I’m having full-on meltdowns, but it’s enough that I plan my routes around it and worry about it more than I think other people do.
